            <h1>The Classical Backpropagation Through Time Factorization</h1>
            <strong>
            TL;DR A derivation of the "classical" factorization of backpropagation through time, as described in <a href="https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-020-17236-y">Bellec et al 2020</a>
            </strong>
            
            <h2>Computation graphs and the chain rule</h2>
            
            <p>
            The rule for computing partial derivatives is to sum up the paths (see <a href="https://colah.github.io/posts/2015-08-Backprop/">Christopher Olah's excellent blog post on this</a>). In the multivariate case, instead of multiplying partial derivatives together we multiply Jacobians.
            </p>
